segments.name: Subscription and support
segments.note: The core software subscriptions — sales, service, Slack, Tableau and now Informatica, which added $440M in the quarter.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Consulting and implementation work that helps customers roll out the software — small, and shrinking slightly.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform, including its Agentforce AI products — up 14% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: The largest running cost — Salesforce's big sales force and marketing machine.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — roughly flat vs a year ago.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: One-off costs of reorganizing teams, up from just $4M a year ago.

oneTimers: A $2,613M gain on strategic investments — a paper (mark-to-market) gain, not cash from customers — accounts for most of the jump in net income from $1,887M to $3,526M.
verdict: Salesforce grew revenue 11% to $11.3B, but the real story is a $2.6B paper gain on its investment portfolio — it more than doubled reported profit while core operating income was flat at $2.3B.
otherDetail: A $2,613M paper gain on strategic investments (Salesforce's stakes in other companies), plus $81M of other income, minus $473M of interest expense.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $1.96 a year ago — lifted by a one-time gain

takeaways.title: Subscriptions keep compounding
takeaways.text: Subscription and support revenue grew 12% to $10.8B — 95% of all revenue — helped by $440M from the newly acquired Informatica.

takeaways.title: A paper gain did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: A $2.6B mark-to-market gain on strategic investments is why GAAP EPS jumped to $4.29 from $1.96. Strip it out and operating income was flat — the gain is real on paper, but it isn't the software business selling more.

takeaways.title: Far fewer shares outstanding
takeaways.text: Buybacks cut the diluted share count from 962M to 821M in a year, so each remaining share claims a bigger slice of the same profit.

follow100Note: Kept-as-profit includes +$19.58 of other income per $100 of revenue; the rows add to $99.99 due to rounding.
